To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the corrosion rate increases with increasing grain size of the nanocoating due to increase in the surface stress, surface modulus, surface porosities and permeability of the nanocoat.

the corrosion rate increased with increasing grain sizes of nanocoatings due to increase in the surface stress, surface elasticity, surface porosity as well as the permeability of nanocomposite coating.
the mechanical parameters of nanocoatings have a significant influence on the corrosion failure.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the corrosion behavior of Ni-based nanocoatings with the aim of understanding the role of intrinsic mechanical parameters on the corrosion rate of nanocoatings and developing a predictive tool to study the corrosion behavior of nanocoatings.
the development of a new approach to the analysis of the corrosion failure of nanostructured materials.
the development of a set of equations to analyze the corrosion behavior of nanocomposite coating.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the corrosion resistance of the nanocoating can be improved by increasing the surface elastic modulus, decreasing the surface porosity and reducing the permeability of the coating.
the surface mechanical properties, such as surface elastic modulus, permeability, grain size and surface stress have significant effect on the corrosion rate of nanocomposite materials.
the corrosion rate increased with increasing surface stress and grain size, while it decreased with increasing surface porosity and surface elastic modulus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the developed equations are able to predict the effects of the intrinsic mechanical parameters on corrosion failure of nanocoatings and the results are in good qualitative agreement with experimental results.
the developed equations can be used for the analysis and modeling of the corrosion behavior of nanocoatings in general and can be extended to other nanocoatings.
the proposed model is capable of predicting the corrosion behavior of nanocomposite coating with a reasonable accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nanocomposite coatings are more sensitive to mechanical parameters than the conventional metallic coatings.
the corrosion rate is directly proportional to the surface stress and permeability of the nanocoating.
the intrinsic mechanical properties of nanocoatings play an important role in the corrosion behavior of the nanocomposite coating.
